channel.title: The Ottawa Citizen - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Ottawa Citizen (ottawacitizen.com)

item.title: OC Transpo acknowledges slow going in O-Train axle repairs
item.description: There are still just 21 train cars available for Line 1 service, while 38 remain out of service for inspection and repairs. Those numbers have remained unchanged for several weeks.

item.title: Ottawa Senators' U.S. Olympians to face off against captain Auston Matthews and the Toronto Maple Leafs
item.description: Gold-medal memories are nice, but both Ottawa and Toronto have to make getting back in the playoff race their priority now.

item.title: Ottawa's PWHL players charged up by relationship with Capital City Condors
item.description: "I said to our team at the end of practice, 'The next 30 minutes is going to be the greatest experience of your week because you get a chance to fill your cup with these passionate hockey players.'"

item.title: Canada's Drug Agency recommends new Alzheimer's drug not be publicly funded
item.description: Dr. Andrew Frank said he is hopeful that the drug will be covered through private health plans. A small number of Canadians are paying for the costly drug themselves.

item.title: Kichesippi Beer Co. shutting its doors in March
item.description: In a statement on the brewery's website, owner Paul Meek said the brewery was operating at a loss and had been "for some time."

item.title: Man and dog rescued from Rideau River in Barrhaven
item.description: Ottawa Fire Services' Ice Rescue Team was called to the scene just past 1:15 p.m. on Saturday.

item.title: Hundreds rally at U.S. Embassy in Ottawa to support military strike on Iran
item.description: The rally was held hours after Israel and the U.S. launched a major attack on Iran on Saturday.

item.title: What we're hearing going into the NHL's trade deadline next Friday
item.description: The new postseason salary cap, taking effect this spring, could affect movement going into the trade deadline.

item.title: How the Ottawa Charge lost to the Boston Fleet despite a dominant performance by Rebecca Leslie
item.description: A defeat in the shootout kept the Charge in fifth place in the standings, one point out of playoff position.

item.title: Ottawa Senators deliver knockout punch to Toronto Maple Leafs in Battle of Ontario
item.description: The victory to start a five-game road trip moved the Senators to within five points of the final wildcard spot in the Eastern Conference of the National Hockey League.
